q: Prugnolo Gentile is the local name for Sangiovese in the wine of which hill town?
exp: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano must be at least seventy percent Sangiovese under that local name. The town has nothing to do with the Montepulciano grape of Abruzzo.

q: A guest cannot see the difference between Montepulciano d'Abruzzo and Vino Nobile di Montepulciano. What should you tell them?
opts: They are the same wine sold under two names
One is sparkling and the other still
One is white and the other red
One names a grape grown in Abruzzo, the other a Tuscan town growing Sangiovese
exp: Montepulciano the variety is planted heavily down the Adriatic side of the country. Montepulciano the town is in southern Tuscany, and its wine is Sangiovese.

q: Cabernet Sauvignon planted near the Tuscan coast made the reputation of which denomination?
exp: Bolgheri sits on the Maremma coast south of Livorno, and the zone launched the Super Tuscan movement. Sassicaia went further in 2013, becoming Bolgheri Sassicaia DOC, Italy's first denomination held by a single estate.

q: Tuscany's only white DOCG grows around a town of medieval towers. Which wine is it?
exp: Vernaccia di San Gimignano was the first wine in Italy to be granted DOC status, in 1966. It remains the region's only white at DOCG level.

q: Sangiovese grown in the warm coastal Maremma carries which denomination name?
exp: Morellino is simply the local name for Sangiovese in that corner of Tuscany. The heat gives a fuller, softer wine than the same grape makes in the hills inland.

q: Dried grapes, small sealed casks and years in a warm loft produce which Tuscan speciality?
exp: Trebbiano and Malvasia are dried, pressed and sealed into caratelli, often with a madre starter from a previous batch. The casks are left through the swings of the seasons.

q: Which region grows Verdicchio in the hills behind Ancona?
exp: Marche faces the Adriatic on the eastern side of the peninsula. Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi and the higher, cooler Verdicchio di Matelica are its two zones for the grape.

q: One of Italy's most tannic red grapes is grown around Montefalco. Which is it?
exp: Sagrantino carries exceptional tannin even by Italian standards and needs long ageing to soften. Montefalco also makes a sweet passito version from the same fruit.

q: Which city has Frascati grown in the volcanic hills immediately outside it?
exp: The Castelli Romani hills southeast of Rome are old volcanic country. Frascati is their Malvasia and Trebbiano based white, historically drunk young in the city.

q: Frizzante red wine served cool alongside rich Emilian cooking comes from which grape?
exp: Lambrusco is a family of related varieties around Modena and Reggio Emilia. The bubbles and acidity are there to cut through the fat of the local food.

q: A pale cherry-coloured rose from Abruzzo carries which denomination name?
exp: Cerasuolo means cherry-coloured. It is made from Montepulciano with only brief skin contact and holds a denomination of its own, separate from the red.

q: Which red variety, grown on volcanic soils in Campania, gives the wine Taurasi?
exp: Aglianico ripens very late and carries firm tannin with high acidity, so it rewards ageing. Taurasi was the first DOCG granted anywhere in southern Italy.

q: Fiano and Greco di Tufo are white denominations of which region?
exp: The hills inland of Naples around Avellino are high and cool. That altitude is why these whites keep structure and can age, unusually for the south.

q: Vineyards on the slopes of an extinct volcano called Vulture grow Aglianico in which region?
exp: Basilicata is mountainous and largely landlocked, and Aglianico del Vulture is effectively its one famous wine. The soils are volcanic ash and lava at real altitude.

q: DNA work matched a widely planted Californian grape to a Puglian variety. Which Italian name does it carry?
exp: Primitivo and Zinfandel proved to be the same variety, traced back to Croatian Tribidrag. Puglia's heat pushes it towards ripe, jammy, high-alcohol styles.

q: Salice Salentino and Negroamaro belong to the heel of Italy. Which region is that?
exp: The Salento peninsula is flat, hot and very dry. Negroamaro and Primitivo dominate its reds, which tend to be soft and warm rather than structured.
